summary: Matthews & Nulty is a small New Jersey CPA firm founded in 1983 by James Matthews and renamed after Michael Nulty became partner in 2015, serving small to mid-size private businesses, non-profits and individuals from offices in East Brunswick and (since late 2023) Hazlet. It sells nine service lines including business and personal tax, audits and reviews, payroll, virtual CFO and HOA accounting. Public reviews are strongly positive on responsiveness and tax knowledge, while the firm's own web presence is thin: one shared phone number for both offices, a contact form rather than online booking, and marketing content and blog posts that have not been updated since 2022-2023.

facts.fact: James Matthews started the practice in 1983 in East Brunswick, NJ; Michael W. Nulty was made partner in early 2015 after seven years working under Matthews. Both are CPAs and graduates of Saint Peter's University.
The firm serves small to mid-size, privately held clients and non-profits, and describes itself as 'CPAs providing peace of mind' with over 35 years of service.

Nine service lines are listed: business taxes, personal taxes, audits & reviews, financial statements, payroll, profitability consulting, virtual CFO services, HOA accounting, and budgeting & money management.

Two offices: Turnpike Plaza, 197 New Jersey 18, Suite 110S, East Brunswick NJ 08816, and 53 Village Court, Hazlet NJ 07730. Both offices list the same phone number, 732-257-8604, and one shared email, info@matthewsandnulty.com.
The Hazlet office was added in late 2023 through a stated partnership with Graziano & Company's Hazlet, NJ branch, whose staff and clients the firm says it will continue to serve.
The site's top bar displays 'Five Star Investment Professional Award Winner 2023', linked to a Five Star Professional spotlight page.

Payroll services advertised include state and federal payroll tax filings, paying payroll tax liabilities, direct deposit, a 'dedicated payroll specialist', and union/certified payroll and workers' comp reporting.

HOA accounting services advertised include audits, compliance, reviews, tax preparation, forensic accounting, transition to unit-owner control, and budgeting/cash-flow planning for New Jersey associations.
A third-party business directory lists the firm at 5.0 stars from 21 reviews with office hours of 9AM-5PM Monday-Friday and closed Saturday and Sunday.
The site's main navigation includes a 'Client Portal' link pointing to matthewsandnulty.clientportal.com, alongside Home, About, Services, QuickBooks ProAdvisor, Blog, Testimonials and Contact.
The blog's most recent post is dated April 21, 2022 ('Tax Deductions VS. Tax Credit'); earlier posts run back to December 2019.
The site footer credits Colossus Media Group (cmg-agency.com) as the site builder, and the page loads Google Tag Manager (GTM-W6J4XWX), Yoast SEO, and WPForms Pro with a math captcha.

operations_signals: New-client intake runs through a WPForms contact form (name, email, phone, service dropdown, message) protected by a simple math captcha; the 'Schedule Consultation' call-to-action on the homepage just links to that contact page, with no online booking calendar anywhere on the site (https://matthewsandnulty.com/contact)

Both offices share one phone number (732-257-8604) and one generic inbox (info@matthewsandnulty.com) — there is no separate Hazlet line, so callers are not routed by location (https://matthewsandnulty.com/contact)

No business hours, after-hours number or emergency contact is published on the firm's own site; hours appear only on third-party directories as Mon-Fri 9AM-5PM, closed weekends (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/east-brunswick/matthews-and-nulty-inc/6592928/)
Client document exchange appears to run through a separate client portal login (clientportal.com) linked in the main navigation, rather than through the public site (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
The homepage and footer newsletter signup is a bare form with no action/handler in the HTML, suggesting it does not actually submit anywhere (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)

Service pages reuse the same 'Who Do We Help?' boilerplate (small business / single-member LLC / S-Corp) across unrelated services like payroll and HOA accounting, and the virtual CFO card on the homepage carries unrelated text about searching a name or phone number — template copy that was never customized (https://matthewsandnulty.com/services/hoa-accounting)
review_themes: Consistent praise for responsiveness and follow-through: reviewers describe prompt appointments and 'follows through with his work' (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/east-brunswick/matthews-and-nulty-inc/6592928/)
Praise for technical depth across individual and business returns and for clear explanations to non-accountants (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/east-brunswick/matthews-and-nulty-inc/6592928/)

The client portal is called out by name as useful by at least one reviewer, indicating clients already work in a self-service document channel (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/east-brunswick/matthews-and-nulty-inc/6592928/)

Firm-published testimonials emphasize delivered savings and credits (payroll tax savings, a health insurance credit) and turnaround on financial statements — outcome-focused rather than process-focused feedback (https://matthewsandnulty.com/testimonials/)
Word-of-mouth is a recurring acquisition source in reviews ('found Mike through word of mouth') (https://www.loc8nearme.com/new-jersey/east-brunswick/matthews-and-nulty-inc/6592928/)
No complaints about missed calls, slow responses or billing errors were found in the accessible review sources; the Yelp listings (East Brunswick and Hazlet) could not be read (see data_gaps)
tech_footprint: Website runs WordPress with Yoast SEO, WPForms Pro (phone masking, math captcha, entry analytics), jQuery and a SiteGround optimizer bundle (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
Google Tag Manager container GTM-W6J4XWX is installed with a noscript fallback (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
An additional third-party tracking script from 240765.tctm.co loads site-wide, pointing to a marketing/attribution vendor rather than a native analytics setup (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
Client portal hosted at matthewsandnulty.clientportal.com, linked from the main navigation (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
Google Maps embeds for both the East Brunswick and Hazlet addresses on the homepage, and a Google Maps link plus a manual address block on the contact page (https://matthewsandnulty.com/contact)
Site is built and maintained by Colossus Media Group, with a co-branded financial-services marketing logo (mccp.services) in the footer (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
Presence on Facebook and LinkedIn (company page ~225 followers per search listing) exists but content is sporadic, and the site blog stopped in April 2022 (https://matthewsandnulty.com/blogs)
growth_signals: Second office opened in Hazlet in late 2023 after partnering with Graziano & Company's Hazlet branch, explicitly framed as inheriting that firm's staff and clients (https://matthewsandnulty.com/hazlet/)

A Graziano & Company business listing states the Hazlet practice was acquired by Mike Nulty, CPA of Matthews & Nulty on October 2, 2023, with staff and location unchanged; the prior Graziano location is now listed as closed (https://fr.yelp.ca/biz/graziano-and-company-cpas-hazlet-2)
Five Star Investment Professional Award 2023 is promoted in the site header, an award used by the firm for local credibility (https://matthewsandnulty.com/)
Service menu expanded to nine lines covering business tax, payroll, audits, virtual CFO and HOA/association accounting — a broader book than a pure tax shop (https://matthewsandnulty.com/services/)

Marketing momentum lags the growth: blog posts end April 2022, the Hazlet announcement (Nov 2023) is the only page updated since, and no job postings or careers page exist (https://matthewsandnulty.com/blogs)
decision_maker: Michael (Mike) Nulty, CPA — Co-founder/Partner; James Matthews, CPA — Co-founder (both listed on the firm's About page, source: https://matthewsandnulty.com/about)

inferences.inference: Inbound client contact is almost certainly handled manually by whoever is at the desk, creating missed-call and slow-first-response risk during filing season.
inferences.reasoning: One shared phone line and one generic inbox serve two offices, there is no online booking or self-service scheduling, and no hours or after-hours coverage is published, so callers have no channel other than a phone call or a web form.

inferences.inference: The 2023 Hazlet acquisition likely created a period of duplicate processes, inconsistent document intake and client-record cleanup across the two offices.
inferences.reasoning: The firm publicly states it absorbed an established practice (Graziano, founded 1985) with its staff and clients, yet still runs both locations off a single phone number and a single contact form with no per-office routing or portal distinction.

inferences.inference: The firm is small — likely under about 10 people, with 1-2 CPAs plus a junior accountant and minimal dedicated administrative staff.
inferences.reasoning: Only two leaders are named on the site; a LinkedIn profile shows a Monmouth University accounting student working as an accountant at the firm; the site has no team page, no careers page, and 2023-era marketing content.

inferences.inference: Marketing and content upkeep is being deferred because billable work takes priority, and the newsletter form is likely broken or unused.
inferences.reasoning: Blog stopped April 2022, service pages carry uncustomized template boilerplate, the virtual CFO blurb is unrelated placeholder text, and the newsletter form has no submit action in the HTML.

inferences.inference: HOA/association clients are the most automation-friendly revenue line: recurring monthly reporting, owner inquiries and board-package assembly are repetitive and deadline-driven.
inferences.reasoning: The firm advertises monthly-style HOA services (budgeting, cash flow, reviews, owner transitions) for multiple associations, which generates high volumes of similar documents and repeat questions rather than one-off advisory work.

inferences.inference: Seasonal staffing strain is concentrated in the Jan-Apr window, when personal returns, business returns and payroll filings collide.
inferences.reasoning: The service mix (individual + business tax + payroll + HOA) all peaks around the same federal deadlines, and no additional staff or seasonal hiring is publicly visible.

inferences.inference: The Suite number for the East Brunswick office is inconsistent across the web (110S on the firm's site vs 202N on directories), which may confuse clients and map listings.
inferences.reasoning: The firm's contact page shows Suite 110S while a directory listing and its snippet show Suite #202N for the same Turnpike Plaza address.

data_gaps: Yelp listings for both offices (https://www.yelp.com/biz/matthews-and-nulty-east-brunswick and /matthews-and-nulty-hazlet) returned HTTP 403 / CAPTCHA, so review text and star ratings could not be read; a search result title indicates 14 reviews on the East Brunswick listing.
BBB search returned only a cookie-consent page; no BBB rating or complaint history captured.

No current or recent job postings found: the site has no careers page (matthewsandnulty.com/careers is 404), and Indeed, ZipRecruiter and LinkedIn job pages returned 403/Cloudflare verification. hiring_signals is therefore empty rather than negative.
Employee headcount is not published anywhere accessible; the size figure is an inference only.
No Google Business Profile rating or review count was captured directly (Google Maps pages would not render); the 5.0/21 figure comes from a third-party directory aggregator.
Business hours are not published on the firm's own site; the 9AM-5PM, Mon-Fri schedule comes from loc8nearme and may be stale.
No local news coverage of the Hazlet acquisition was located beyond the firm's own Hazlet page and Graziano's own business listing.
ProvenExpert profile exists for the Hazlet location but the page body returned only cookie-consent text, so its ratings are unknown.
Fees, engagement minimums, client counts and revenue are not disclosed.
